title: Normalizing the discrete Gaussian sampler loop by a chain of rewrites
intent: Prove that the discrete Gaussian sampler loop is a proper distribution (its mass sums to 1) by a chain of rewrites: replace the mixed Laplace sampler by its equivalence, drop the two off-diagonal if-guarded masses with the same-file ite_simpl lemmas, fold the Boolean sum with the Bernoulli normalization lemma, and close the remaining factor with the Laplace normalization lemma.

parent.name: DiscreteGaussianSampleLoop_normalizes
parent.statement:
theorem DiscreteGaussianSampleLoop_normalizes (num den t : ℕ+) (mix : ℕ) :
  ∑' x, (DiscreteGaussianSampleLoop num den t mix) x = 1

children.name: DiscreteLaplaceSampleMixed_equiv
children.statement:
lemma DiscreteLaplaceSampleMixed_equiv (num den : PNat) (mix : ℕ) :
    DiscreteLaplaceSampleMixed num den mix = DiscreteLaplaceSample num den
children.closed_by: rw [DiscreteLaplaceSampleMixed]; split; the mix=true goal is rfl, the mix=false goal is symm; apply DiscreteLaplaceSample_equiv

children.name: ite_simpl_gaussian_1
children.statement:
lemma ite_simpl_gaussian_1 (num den t: ℕ+) (x a : ℤ) :
  @ite ENNReal (x = a) (propDecidable (x = a)) 0
  (if a = x then
    DiscreteLaplaceSample t 1 x *
      BernoulliExpNegSample (Int.natAbs (Int.sub (|x| * ↑↑t * ↑↑den) ↑↑num) ^ 2) (2 * num * t ^ 2 * den) false
  else 0) = 0
children.closed_by: split; simp; then split on the inner if: the a = x branch is rename_i h1 h2; subst h2; contradiction, the other branch is simp

children.name: ite_simpl_gaussian_2
children.statement:
lemma ite_simpl_gaussian_2 (num den t: ℕ+) (x a : ℤ) :
  @ite ENNReal (x = a) (propDecidable (x = a)) 0
  (if a = x then
    DiscreteLaplaceSample t 1 x *
      BernoulliExpNegSample (Int.natAbs (Int.sub (|x| * ↑↑t * ↑↑den) ↑↑num) ^ 2) (2 * num * t ^ 2 * den) true
  else 0) = 0
children.closed_by: split; simp; then split on the inner if: the a = x branch is rename_i h1 h2; subst h2; contradiction, the other branch is simp

children.name: BernoulliExpNegSample_normalizes
children.statement:
theorem BernoulliExpNegSample_normalizes (num : Nat) (den : PNat) :
  (∑' b : Bool, (BernoulliExpNegSample num den) b) = 1
children.closed_by: unfold BernoulliExpNegSample; split on num ≤ den; the first branch is have A := BernoulliExpNegSampleUnit_normalizes, the second branch proves a local e1 then have B := BernoulliExpNegSampleGenLoop_normalizes

children.name: DiscreteLaplaceSample_normalizes
children.statement:
theorem DiscreteLaplaceSample_normalizes (num den : PNat) :
    ∑' x : ℤ, (DiscreteLaplaceSample num den) x = 1
children.closed_by: have hloop_norm := DiscreteLaplaceSampleLoop_normalizes; simp and probUntil_apply_norm reduce the product; a local hfactor rewrites the ite; ENNReal.tsum_mul_right and ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel close the sum

applicability.goal_shape: ∑' x, (loop sampler) x = 1 where the sampler is a bind of two primitive samplers; the proof is a chain of rewrites that (i) replaces a mixed definition by an equivalent simpler one, (ii) eliminates if-guarded off-diagonal masses, (iii) folds a two-point Boolean sum into a normalization lemma, and (iv) closes the remaining factor with another normalization lemma.
applicability.use_when: each simplification step is exactly one rewrite whose lemma is already proved and named; the sampler is built from components whose normalization lemmas already exist (Bernoulli, Laplace); the off-diagonal terms are if-expressions that a small ite_simpl lemma can kill.
applicability.avoid_when: a step needs several lemmas at once or a have sub-proof (then the child is not a one-line rewrite); the normalizer lemmas have mismatched hypotheses; a factor needs its own non-trivial bound rather than an already-proved = 1.

consequences: The chain creates four obligations, each discharged by one named lemma: bridge the two definitions of the Laplace sampler (DiscreteLaplaceSampleMixed_equiv); show two off-diagonal if-guarded masses are zero (ite_simpl_gaussian_1, ite_simpl_gaussian_2); fold a two-point Boolean sum to 1 (BernoulliExpNegSample_normalizes); close the remaining ℤ sum (DiscreteLaplaceSample_normalizes). Failure modes: the ite_simpl lemmas match the exact @ite shape of the unfolded sampler, so a change to the sampler definition or to the simp normal form breaks the rw; the conv blocks target a fixed position (arg 1; ext a), so reordering the sum or the product factors moves the target and each rw lands on the wrong subterm.
